subject: GitOps: private deployment TF/Helm modules + CI gating review
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@acmehealth.com
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:23:00 -0800
Subject: GitOps: private deployment TF/Helm modules + CI gating review

Hi team — looping you in on an initial review request from Acme Health (cc'd). They want a private deployment behind their VPC with HSM/KMS integration, strict Egress rules, and a GitOps-driven CI gating policy before we hand off the on-prem bundle.

Attachments: tfmodules-network-v1.patch, helm-values-acme-staging.yaml, ci-pipeline-gating.yml (stubs attached)

High-level asks for this thread:
- Review Terraform modules for VPC peering, subnet layout, and NAT/egress NAT gateway rules (security posture must match Acme's baseline).
- Validate Helm chart values for private mode (service annotations, internal loadbalancer, TLS termination disabled on LB).
- CI gating checklist: terraform plan+policy (OPA/Conftest), helm lint + chart-testing, container image SBOM and vulnerability scan, sandbox e2e smoke run.
- Confirm KMS/HSM key policy mapping and where customer-managed keys need to be referenced in the TF modules.

Timeline: Acme would like a consolidated review notes by EOD Tuesday (11/17). Can we each take scope ownership? I'll kick off the PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy/pull/284

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.ai, soojin.lee@redwood.ai, ops@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: GitOps: private deployment TF/Helm modules + CI gating review

Karthik — thanks for pulling this together. Quick notes after skimming the TF patch (see inline below).

> From the patch: vpc_network module creates 2 public + 3 private subnets per AZ
- Recommend: default to 1 public + N private by region; Acme's security policy forbids internet-facing SNAT from private subnets. We should present a nat-radius option (managed NAT gateway vs egress-only NAT via managed proxy).

> Security groups: broad port 443 ingress on internalLB
- Suggest locking to application CIDR and ALB health-check CIDR ranges; add explicit description tags.

> Outputs: no peering route table id exported
- Need to export peering_connection_id and route_table_ids so the peering job in the downstream repo can stitch routes. Also add a module-level variable to opt into cross-account peering.

CI gating: the ci-pipeline-gating.yml should include an OPA step (policy repo link) and a terraform fmt/validate stage before plan. Linting alone is insufficient. For helm we should add chart-testing with kubeconform for CRD validation.

I'll take the TF networking module owner for the PR and push a small patch tomorrow morning. Marcus, can you cover the Helm values + default secret handling? Soojin — can you confirm SOC2-alignment for the egress controls and whether the retention policy on KMS keys meets Acme's audit requirements?

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Director, Cloud Solutions
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai

On Sun, 15 Nov 2026 at 09:23, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi team — looping you in on an initial review request from Acme Health (cc'd). They want a private deployment behind their VPC with HSM/KMS integration...
From: Ops Team <ops@acmehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: certs@venclave.com, sre-team@fincloud.io
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 13:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: GitOps: private deployment TF/Helm modules + CI gating review

Thanks Karthik and Lauren — we appreciate the clear checklist. A couple of questions from Acme infra:

1) HSM/KMS: Our HSM vendor (Venclave, cc'd) requires an initial CSR workflow and an HSM policy that references private key endpoints. Where exactly will the TF module expose the key alias and IAM role mapping? Will Redwood expect us to create the KMS keys and hand you the ARN, or should the TF module create the keys in our account?

2) Certificates: given TLS termination is customer-side, we need a documented path to rotate certs without downtime. Can the Helm chart support a TLS secret reload hook and we can run a cert-manager job in the platform?

3) Staging window: we prefer a deploy window Thurs 11/19 02:00-06:00 UTC for staging validation. Is that workable for Redwood's side?

Attachment: helm-values-acme-staging.yaml (values file stub)

—Acme Ops
ops@acmehealth.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@acmehealth.com, certs@venclave.com
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: GitOps: private deployment TF/Helm modules + CI gating review

All — quick consolidation and action items before Tuesday EOD as requested by Acme:

Action owners:
- TF network module (karthik): add optional managed-proxy egress mode, export peering ids, and parameterize nat strategy. Will open PR with tfmodules-network-v1.patch (done).
- Helm values (marcus): add TLS secret reload hooks, document cert-manager compatibility, and ensure chart-testing passes with kubeconform.
- Compliance check (soojin): verify KMS key rotation/retention meets SOC2 and produce a short checklist for Acme's audit team.
- CI gating (lauren): add OPA policy step, terraform fmt/validate, and a sandbox e2e smoke job in the pipeline.

Answers to Acme questions (quick):
- KMS/HSM: We recommend customer-managed keys. TF modules will accept a kms_key_arn variable; we will not create customer KMS keys unless explicitly requested in the SOW. Venclave — please share the CSR workflow docs and required ARN patterns.
- TLS/certs: Helm chart will include a post-deploy hook template that triggers a rollout if secret contents change; we'll document the cert-manager job pattern in Confluence.
- Staging window Thursday 11/19 02:00-06:00 UTC is acceptable; I'll book the CI runners and a Redwood engineer to monitor.

References: PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy/pull/284, Confluence draft https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/PrivDeploy+TF+Module+standards, Jira JIRA-PRIV-712 (tracking).

I'll follow up after Marcus pushes the Helm changes and after Soojin confirms KMS retention language. Thanks everyone — aiming to have the consolidated notes and a green CI run by Thu staging.

Karthik
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
